## Natural history notes

A native creeping perennial herb characterized by round, shield-like leaves held on upright stalks, giving the foliage the appearance of tiny parasols. Whorled Pennywort spreads by slender rhizomes and produces inconspicuous greenish-white flowers in small whorled clusters along short flowering stalks. In Florida, it occurs in wet, open habitats such as marshes, wet prairies, pond margins, ditches, and seasonally flooded flatwoods. It tolerates saturated soils and shallow flooding and can form low mats along wetland edges, where it contributes groundcover and habitat structure for small aquatic and terrestrial organisms.
